fact: Every NCA exam is taken online, on your own computer at home, with a proctor watching. It is open book.
You can bring books to an NCA exam, but only paper ones. Electronic copies are not allowed.
The pass mark for an NCA exam is 50 percent.
The NCA holds an exam session every month, but each core subject comes round only every third month. Plan around that.

fact: Each NCA exam is three hours long and is typed on your computer.

fact: The NCA assessment costs CAD 400 and each exam costs CAD 500, plus Canadian taxes.
The fastest path to the NCA Certificate of Qualification is about 10 months. The usual path takes about two years.
You get five years from your assessment date to finish your NCA exams.
NCA results come about 10 to 12 weeks after the last exam of the session.
Since 1 March 2026 every NCA applicant must pass a language screening before the assessment decision.
The English screening is one proctored test, with a score of 61 needed, equal to IELTS 7. You get one attempt, and its cost is inside the assessment fee.
A recent IELTS, CELPIP or PTE result, less than two years old, can replace the English screening.
A new Indigenous law requirement began on 1 March 2026. It is a six week online course from CPLED.
The NCA Certificate of Qualification says your Canadian law knowledge is similar to a Canadian law graduate's.
The Certificate of Qualification is not a law degree and does not admit you to the bar. A provincial law society licenses lawyers.

fact: After the NCA you apply to a provincial law society. This works in every common law province and territory, but not in Quebec.
The Certificate of Qualification never expires, but each law society limits how long you can wait before you start its licensing process.
Canada outside Quebec uses common law, like India, so the way of reasoning in the exams will feel familiar.

The NCA assigns most applicants at least five core exams: constitutional law, administrative law, criminal law, professional responsibility and foundations of Canadian law. Your own list depends on your degree.
